schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: go-rclone-sftp-powershell-incomplete-quote-escape
title: PowerShell path quoting only doubles ASCII apostrophe, allowing smart-quote command injection
summary: A path is wrapped in single quotes for PowerShell and only the ASCII apostrophe is escaped with
  strings.ReplaceAll. PowerShell also treats the Unicode smart quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B
  as single-quote delimiters. A crafted filename can therefore close the string literal and inject arbitrary
  PowerShell statements on the remote host.
cwe:
- CWE-78
severity: high
confidence: high
languages:
- go
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: e122fba1a57641b63a580aa26c026903a84e2e88
  vulnerable_ref: e122fba1a57641b63a580aa26c026903a84e2e88^
  patched_ref: e122fba1a57641b63a580aa26c026903a84e2e88
  repository: https://github.com/rclone/rclone
rule:
  message: 'Path is quoted for PowerShell by escaping only the ASCII apostrophe. PowerShell also treats
    the Unicode smart quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B as quote delimiters, so a crafted filename
    can break out of the literal and inject commands. Double all of these characters, for example with
    a strings.NewReplacer.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: '"''" + strings.ReplaceAll($S, "''", "''''") + "''"

        '
    - pattern: '"''" + strings.Replace($S, "''", "''''", -1) + "''"

        '
    - pattern: '"''" + strings.NewReplacer("''", "''''").Replace($S) + "''"

        '
fix:
  guidance: Escape every character PowerShell accepts as a single-quote delimiter, not just the ASCII
    apostrophe. Use a strings.NewReplacer that doubles ', U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B, and wrap
    the result in apostrophes. Doubling a delimiter is PowerShell's escape for a literal occurrence of
    it.
  example: "var powerShellQuoteEscaper = strings.NewReplacer(\n    \"'\", \"''\",\n    \"\\u2018\", \"\
    \\u2018\\u2018\",\n    \"\\u2019\", \"\\u2019\\u2019\",\n    \"\\u201A\", \"\\u201A\\u201A\",\n  \
    \  \"\\u201B\", \"\\u201B\\u201B\",\n)\n\nfunc quotePS(p string) string {\n    return \"'\" + powerShellQuoteEscaper.Replace(p)\
    \ + \"'\"\n}\n"
